name: 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum Auffach
kurzbeschreibung: The 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum in Auffach (Wildschönau): over 3,000 carved wooden exhibits in the birthplace of woodcarver Hubert Salcher.
beschreibung:
Overview

The 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum is located in the picturesque mountain village of Auffach in the heart of the Wildschönau high valley (Kufstein district) at an altitude of around 875 metres. Housed in a more than 300-year-old, heritage-protected Tyrolean log house – the birthplace of the renowned Wildschönau woodcarver and artist Hubert Salcher –, the museum ranks among the most unique and charming specialist museums in the entire Alpine region. Across more than 1,000 square metres of exhibition space and in over 30 rustic parlours and chambers, the museum showcases the fascinating cultural history of wood as a material and centuries of Alpine craftsmanship traditions.

Exhibition & Wooden Masterpieces

The private museum was founded in 1996 by Hubert Salcher himself, who transformed his historic family home into a treasure trove of Alpine folk culture through decades of dedicated collecting and restoration work. Featuring more than 3,000 original wooden exhibits, the museum documents the indispensable role wood played in the survival and daily livelihood of Tyrolean mountain farmers over five centuries. Notable highlights include Tyrol's oldest wooden drilling machine, historic wooden sledges, intricately carved cradles, ornate wooden clocks, traditional tools of coopers, cartwrights, and carpenters, as well as a completely furnished historical shoemaker's workshop. Special attention is given to the sacred and secular carvings by Hubert Salcher himself: his finely detailed reliefs, life-sized statues of saints, and whimsical wooden sculptures demonstrate masterful artistry. On the upper floor, a dedicated section traces the history of Wildschönau timber rafting and forestry. For his life's work and the preservation of rural cultural heritage, the museum has received multiple regional heritage and cultural awards.

Visit & Getting There

The 1. Tiroler Holzmuseum is open during the summer season from mid-May to late October from Wednesday to Friday from 10:00 to 17:00 (accessible on additional weekdays on public holidays and for registered groups of 10 or more; winter tours available upon advance booking). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €9.00, seniors approx. €8.00, children and teenagers (6 to 15 years) approx. €4.50, family ticket approx. €20.00. Holders of the regional Wildschönau Card receive a discount. Arrival by car: Via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl Ost), continuing on the Wildschönauer Landesstraße L15 via Niederau and Oberau to Auffach; free parking spaces are available directly at the museum (Dorf Auffach 148). By public transport: ÖBB train to Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, from where VVT bus line 4064 runs hourly directly to the Auffach Holzmuseum stop.

Tips

The ground floor of the museum offers step-free access; the upper floors of the 300-year-old wooden house are accessible via historic wooden stairs. When present in person, museum carver Hubert Salcher gladly guides guests through the rooms himself and demonstrates traditional carving techniques in his open workshop. Combine your museum visit with a ride on the nearby Schatzbergbahn cable car up to over 1,900 metres above sea level.
